sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:5657
Court No. - 89
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 42379 of 2023
Applicant :- Parveen Nikhat And Another
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and

Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Udai Prakash Deo Pandey

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mrs. Sadhna Rani (Thakur),J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

By moving this application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., the prayer is made to quash the order dated 20.08.2022 passed by the Civil Judge (S.D.)/A.C.J.M., Sonbhadra, District Sonbhadra in Case No.13/2021, arising out of Complaint No.2340/2016, Shaheen Parveen Vs. Irfan Ahmad and others,
under Sections 498A, 323, 504 I.P.C. & under Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
By impugned order, the trial court allowed

entities.text: Shaheen Parveen Vs. Irfan Ahmad and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the application of the opposite party no.2 moved under Section 319 of Cr.P.C. and summoned the applicant no.1- Parveen Nikhat to face trial under Sections 498A, 323, 504 IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act and applicant no.2- Mohd. Shakir to face trial under Sections 498A IPC and 3/4 of D.P. Act.

It is argued by the learned counsel for the applicants that in the statement under Section 200 Parveen Nikhat And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166467348/
1 Cr.P.C. of the complainant/ opposite party no.2, there is no allegation against applicant no.1- Parveen Nikhat.
Applicant no.1 is the married sister-in-law of the opposite party no.2 having two children.
Applicant no.2 lives in Jharkhand 200 kilometres away from the parental house of the opposite party no.2.
Both of them have no role in the incident.
The whole family has been implicated in the matter.
Applicant no.2 was the mediator of the marriage, so he has also been falsely implicated.

The complaint was filed on 09.11.2016 and this application under Section 319 of Cr.P.C.
was moved on 10.03.2022, which has been allowed on 20.08.2022, hence, the prayer is made accordingly.
Learned A.G.A., however, opposed the prayer and submitted that the process under Section 82/83 of Cr.P.C. has been issued against the applicants vide order dated 21.07.2023.
The applicants are not appearing in the trial court.
The trial court has passed the order on the basis of the evidence on record, hence, the prayer is made to dismiss this application.

Regarding non- appearance of the applicants in the court, it is submitted that as both the applicants live far away from the court, which passed the order hence, they could not get any information of the process issued against them and thus could not appear before the court in time.

So far as the impugned order is concerned, the impugned order is appended at pages-64 and 65 of the paper book passed on application paper no.76ba of opposite party no.2 appended at page-58 of the paper book.

Admittedly, as per Section 319 of Cr.P.C. the application under this section can be moved, where, in the course of any inquiry into, or trial of, an offence, it appears from the evidence that any person not being the accused has committed any offence for which such person could be tried together with the accused, the Court may proceed against such persons for the offence which he appears to have committed.

Admittedly, this application under Section 319 of Cr.P.C. by the opposite party no.2 was moved in the trial court after the statements of the alleged victim, his brother and father under Section 244 of Cr.P.C.
It is true that in the complaint there is allegation against the applicant no.1- Parveen Nikhat that she specifically demanded a gold chain from the victim and on 16.10.2016, applicant no.2, who is said to be the mediator of the marriage alongwith the brother-in-law of opposite party no.2 reached at the parental house of the opposite party no.2 and demanded a four wheeler and gold chain and when this demand was refused they are said to have hurled wild abuses and given threat of life.
If we go through the statement of the alleged victim under Section 200 of Cr.P.C., wherein she has specifically named applicant no.2- Mohd. Shakir about his visiting her parental house and demanding a car but in her statement under Section 200 of Cr.P.C., she has not specifically named applicant no.1 making a certain demand of gold chain for her.

Again, if we go through the statement of the victim under Section 244 of Cr.P.C. therein she has made a general allegation against all her in-laws regarding demand of car and gold chain and the applicant no.1 has nowhere specifically said to have demanded a gold chain from the victim.

Though, in the statement under Section 244 of Cr.P.C. of the victim, the incident dated 16.10.2016 is there that on this date applicant no.2 Parveen Nikhat And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166467348/
2 alongwith Shane Ahmad came to the parental house of the opposite party no.2 and made a demand of dowry and on refusal, they are said to have abused and given threat of second marriage of the husband of the opposite party no.2.

entities.text: Parveen Nikhat And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mohd. Gufran, the brother of the victim has also not named applicant no.1 in his statement that specifically she made a specific demand of gold chain, from the opposite party no.2, though, the father of the complainant in his statement under Section 244 of Cr.P.C. has mentioned regarding specific demand of gold chain by applicant no.1 but it is clear from the above discussion that the statements of rest witnesses may be the hearsay statements but the real victim is opposite party no.2, who neither in her statement under Section 200 of Cr.P.C., nor in the statement under Section 244 of Cr.P.C. has specifically named the applicant no.1 making demand of gold chain for herself rather there is general allegation of opposite party no.2 in her statements regarding demand of gold chain and car by all her in-laws.
Though, there is specific allegation against the applicant no.2 of arriving at her parental house on 16.10.2016 at 8:00 PM and demanding a four wheeler, hurling wild abuses and giving threat of life.
The applicant no.1 is said to be eldest sister-in-law of opposite party no.2 and a married lady having two children.
It has not come in the evidence anywhere that at the time of marriage of the opposite party no.2 the applicant no.1 was living in her parental house.

If we go through the impugned order, the trial court summoned applicant no.1 on the general allegation regarding demand of dowry by all the in-laws of the opposite party no.2 including applicant no.1- Parveen Nikhat.

For Section 319 of Cr.P.C. in paragraph-106 of judgment in Hardeep Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2014) 3 SCC 92, it has been opined that under Section 319 of Cr.P.C. the test has to be applied is one which is more than prima-facie case as exercised at the time of framing of charge but short of satisfaction to an extent that the evidence if any unrebutted would lead conviction and in absence of such satisfaction the court should refrain from exercising such power under Section 319 Cr.P.C.

entities.text: Hardeep Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2014) 3 SCC 92
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In judgment passed in Criminal Appeal No.875 of 2021- Manjeet Singh Vs. State of Haryana & others, the Apex Court held that only the evidence before the trial court is sufficient enough to exercise the discretion by the court under Section 319 of Cr.P.C.

entities.text: Manjeet Singh Vs. State of Haryana & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the opinion of the Court, that specific evidence against applicant no.1 is missing, while against applicant no.2 there is intact allegation of the opposite party no.2 and her witnesses that he visited the house of the alleged victim on 16.10.2016 and demanded a four wheeler.

In the opinion of the Court, on the basis of evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 the order of the trial court is not sustainable against applicant no.1-Parveen Nikhat, while regarding applicant no.2 being a clear allegation against him in all the statement of the witnesses the order under Section 319 Cr.P.C.
deserves to be confirmed.
The application under section 482 of Cr.P.C. is, thus, allowed partly.
The order dated 20.08.2022 is set aside with regard to applicant no.1- Parveen Nikhat and it is confirmed with regard to applicant no.2- Mohd. Shakir.
